name: NanoDet-Plus m 1.5x 416
about: Object detector for the 80 COCO classes. Describes everything the code needs to know about this one model, so the C++ only holds the algorithm. Each setting has a value, what it means, and where it comes from.

modelFile.about: The ONNX file, in this same folder. Not in git: scripts/fetch-assets.sh downloads it and checks its SHA-256.

size.about: Width and height of the image the model takes, in pixels.

channelOrder.about: Color channel order the model was trained with. NanoDet's training loads images with OpenCV (cv2.imread), which returns BGR. Our camera frames are BGR too, so no conversion is needed. (The Model Zoo demo converts to RGB, which doesn't match training.)

resize.about: How a frame is fitted to the input size. letterbox: shrink keeping the aspect ratio and pad the rest with zeros (what the Model Zoo demo does). stretch: resize to exactly the input size (what NanoDet's config does, keep_ratio: False). The model was trained with random stretching, so it copes with either; we follow the Model Zoo, whose code targets OpenCV DNN like ours.

mean.about: Per-channel average subtracted from each pixel, in B, G, R order: normalized = (pixel - mean) / std. These are ImageNet's dataset means [0.485, 0.456, 0.406] (R, G, B on a 0..1 scale) times 255, reversed to BGR. NanoDet uses ImageNet's statistics because its ShuffleNetV2 backbone starts from ImageNet-pretrained weights.

std.about: Per-channel standard deviation each pixel is divided by, in B, G, R order. ImageNet's [0.229, 0.224, 0.225] (R, G, B, 0..1 scale) times 255, reversed to BGR.

strides.about: The model predicts on grids at three scales. A stride is how many input pixels one grid cell covers: 416 / 8 = 52x52 cells for small objects, 26x26 and 13x13 for larger ones. NanoDet's config lists a fourth stride (64), but this ONNX export only has outputs for these three (see ObjectDetectorTest.GivenTheModel_WhenListingOutputs_ThenThereAreTwoPerStride).

regMax.about: Each box edge's distance from its cell is predicted as a probability over regMax + 1 = 8 bins (0..7 cells), not as one number. The decoder takes the expected value of that distribution. So each cell has 4 edges x 8 bins = 32 box values.

scoreThreshold.about: Minimum confidence (0..1) for a detection to be kept. The OpenCV Model Zoo's default.

nmsThreshold.about: Non-maximum suppression: when two boxes of the same object overlap by more than this (intersection over union, 0..1), only the higher-scoring one is kept. The OpenCV Model Zoo's default.

classes.about: Class names in the order of the model's score outputs: score index 0 is person, 79 is toothbrush. The 80 COCO object classes.
